newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canada official sees no early Peru breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: Canada official sees no early Peru breakthrough.

text.p: Canada's foreign minister said on Friday he saw no early solution to the hostage standoff at Japan's mission in Peru, but underscored his government's willingness to help resolve the crisis.
"I don't see any breakthrough," Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy told a news conference at the end of his 24-hour visit to Japan.

"There is no magic answer" without progress in talks between the Peruvian government and Marxist guerillas who have held 72 hostages the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima since December 17, he said.
Canada's ambassador to Peru, Anthony Vincent, is a member of the three-man mediation team which has held frequent but so far fruitless talks with the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
The mediators met for several hours with the guerrillas on Wednesday inside the residence. But there is no date for a resumption of direct talks with the government.

Axworthy, who arrived in Japan from China on Thursday, held talks with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and other Japanese officials. He was to fly to Hong Kong later on Friday.
